chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Ubayn, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the man who is claimed against (defendant), and there is no proof for the claimant.
He (peace be upon him) said: 'Either he swears an oath or he turns the oath to be upon the owner of the right. So if he does not do it, so there is no right for him'.

key_terms.يُسْتَحْلَفُ: he is made to swear an oath

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when a claimant has no proof against a defendant in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Kafi establishes the principle of *qasam* (oath) as a decisive evidentiary tool in Shia jurisprudence when *bayyinah* (proof) is absent. It highlights the defendant's strategic choice to either swear to their innocence or force the claimant to swear, reflecting the procedural flexibility designed to resolve disputes with minimal burden. The dismissal upon refusal underscores the necessity of active participation in the oath-taking process to validate or invalidate the claim.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Al Qasim Bin Suleyman, from Ubeyd Bin Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding the man who is claimed against (defendant), and there is no proof for the claimant.
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Either he swears an oath or he turns the oath to be upon the owner of the right. So if he does not do it, so there is no right for him’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurarah who has narrated the following: “About the case of a man who brings a complaint against another but does not have testimony, abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘He must ask him (defendant) to take an oath, and if he turns the oath on the plaintiff who does not take the oath, then he has no right.’”
